question: Brazil Presidential Election First Round: 2nd Place
resolution_criteria:
A presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 4, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the listed candidate who receives the second-most valid votes in the first round of this election.

The named candidates will be primarily ranked by the number of valid votes received in the specified election. If two or more candidates are tied on valid votes, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the candidates' last names. This market will resolve to the candidate that occupies the second-highest finishing position after applying this ranking.

If the result of this election isn't known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

"Other" means any option not listed here.
research:
**Bottom line:** As of mid-September 2026, the race for 2nd place is between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, and Flávio is ahead on that question. Datafolha's poll released September 17 had Lula first with 39% and Flávio second with 36%, inside the 2-point margin of error. Flávio has been second in every Datafolha and Quaest national poll I found from August through mid-September. The nearest other candidate polls around 6%. Nothing has settled the question yet; the vote is on 2026-10-04.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on credible reporting of valid votes in the first round. If reporting is ambiguous, the official TSE results decide ([dadosabertos.tse.jus.br](https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/)). No first-round results exist before the October 4 vote.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles it yet.
- On the listed options, as far as I could tell:
  - Tarcísio de Freitas, Michelle Bolsonaro, Fernando Haddad and Jair Bolsonaro do not appear in the September 2026 candidate lists.
  - Jair Bolsonaro is ineligible.
  - The live options appear to be Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro and Renan Santos. A third-place finisher such as Augusto Cury or Ronaldo Caiado would resolve "Other".
- 2026-09-17: Datafolha (fieldwork Sep 15-17, n=2,002, ±2 pp, TSE registration BR-04029/2026) had Lula 39%, Flávio 36%, Augusto Cury 6%, Caiado 4%, Renan Santos 3% and Zema 2%. [Money Times](https://www.moneytimes.com.br/pesquisa-datafolha-17-de-setembro-de-2026-gaep/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-17: The Datafolha poll above had Lula 39%, Flávio 36%. The second-round simulation stayed at 46% to 44%. [Money Times](https://www.moneytimes.com.br/pesquisa-datafolha-17-de-setembro-de-2026-gaep/)
- 2026-09-11: Datafolha had Lula 39%, Flávio 35% in the first round and 46% to 44% in the runoff. [Investidor10](https://investidor10.com.br/noticias/datafolha-flavio-encurta-distancia-e-chega-a-35-contra-39-de-lula-122594/), [Brasil de Fato](https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/09/11/datafolha-lula-tem-39-flavio-bolsonaro-35-no-primeiro-turno/)
- Around 2026-09-13: Quaest (fieldwork Sep 10-13) had Lula 36%, Flávio 31%, Caiado 4%, Renan Santos 4%. This comes from Wikipedia's polling table; I did not find the original Quaest release. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opinion_polling_for_the_2026_Brazilian_presidential_election)
- Around 2026-09-06: Quaest (fieldwork Sep 3-6) had Lula 36%, Flávio 29%, Cury 8%, Caiado 3%, Renan 3%. Also from the Wikipedia table. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opinion_polling_for_the_2026_Brazilian_presidential_election)
- 2026-09-03: Datafolha had Lula 38%, Flávio 33%. [Money Times](https://www.moneytimes.com.br/datafolha-3-de-setembro-gaep/), [Diário do Nordeste](https://diariodonordeste.verdesmares.com.br/pontopoder/pesquisa-datafolha-lula-tem-38-de-intencao-de-voto-no-1-turno-e-flavio-bolsonaro-33-1.3789279)
- 2026-08-14: Quaest (fieldwork Aug 10-12) had Lula 38%, Flávio 31%, Renan Santos 4%, Caiado 4%, Zema 2%, Cury 2%, and 10% undecided. [Metrópoles](https://www.metropoles.com/brasil/quaest-lula-e-flavio-bolsonaro-1o-turno)

## 4. Base rates
- Trend: since early September Flávio has narrowed Lula's lead in Datafolha from 5 points to 3. Flávio is about 30 points clear of third place, so the realistic contest for 2nd is between him and Lula.
- First-round polling misses: in 2022 the final polls understated Jair Bolsonaro by several points. He got 43.2% against roughly 36-38% in final polls, while Lula came first with 48.4%. A late swing of 3 or more points between the top two is therefore historically plausible. This is my general knowledge; I did not fetch a source for it.
- Since the PT/PSDB era began in 1994, every first round except 2018 had two dominant candidates. The top two have always been at least 15 points clear of third place, except in 2002 and 2014.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket has this exact market, "Brazil Presidential Election First Round: 2nd Place". Third-party mirrors show snapshots of Flávio at about 74-77% around late July 2026, and Renan Santos at about 11-16% in one mirror snapshot. These snapshots are inconsistent and their dates are unclear. I could not get a reliable price as of 2026-09-18; the lines.com page returned 403 Forbidden. [Polyguana](https://polyguana.com/events/brazil-presidential-election-first-round-2nd-place), [Predscope](https://predscope.com/event/brazil-presidential-election-first-round-2nd-place), [lines.com](https://www.lines.com/prediction-markets/elections/brazil-presidential-election-first-round-2nd-place)
- I did not find Kalshi or Manifold prices or expert model forecasts for 2nd place specifically.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- More weekly Datafolha and Quaest national polls, plus others such as AtlasIntel, through the campaign's final weekend (October 2-3).
- The final TV debates, and any late tactical-voting shift from Cury, Caiado or Renan Santos voters toward Flávio.
- 2026-10-04: First-round vote. The TSE count is usually decisive on election night (October 4-5), and the question resolves around 2026-10-05.
- What drives the outcome: Lula and Flávio are within the margin of error. If Flávio ends up with more valid votes than Lula, Lula becomes 2nd. If the current order holds, Flávio is 2nd.

- A much less likely surprise is a third candidate overtaking one of the top two, such as Cury surging (which would resolve "Other"). The listed non-candidates (Tarcísio, Michelle, Haddad, Jair) would only matter if a candidate were replaced late, which is very unlikely.

**How I moved:** I started from the status quo, where Flávio is 2nd, at roughly 75%. I moved down to about 62% because of:
- the narrowing trend;
- the record of right-wing candidates beating their polls;
- the tactical-vote pool that could push Flávio into first.
